summary.title: ConnectED
summary.description:
ConnectED is an offline-first examination management PWA for Kenyan schools. This model covers the teacher app and its sync layer, the Laravel API, the admin panel, the queue worker, the model provider, and production on AWS as declared in infra/.

Data subjects are students (mostly minors), teachers, and admins. Parents and students are not users: they receive a printed or forwarded report card and are outside the diagrams.

The institution boundary is logical, not drawn: every institution shares one database and one API, separated by institution_id under an Eloquent global scope.

Each element is modelled, and carries its threats, on exactly one diagram. Where it appears on another it is dashed and marked out of scope with a pointer to its home diagram. The diagrams are of the Generic type so that STRIDE and LINDDUN threats sit on the same elements.

Sources: docs/spec/, docs/adr/ 0001, 0002, 0006, 0007, 0009 to 0015, api/routes/api.php, and frontend/src/lib/localDatabase.ts.

diagrams.title: 1. Teacher device and sync
diagrams.description: The offline-first path: the local store, the outbox, the sync runner, and the server side that accepts or rejects a write. This is the project's contribution and gets the most attention in the STRIDE pass.

data.name: Teacher device (browser, often offline)
data.description: A teacher's own phone or laptop. Not managed by the school, may be shared or lost, and holds a copy of the institution's data. The server treats every value that leaves it as a claim.

data.name: AWS account, af-south-1
data.description: Production as declared in infra/ (ADR 0015). Reached from the internet only through CloudFront.

data.name:
Teacher
(incl. HOD, DOS)
data.description: A teacher account (ADR 0014). Reads everything in the institution and may grade anything. HOD (subject moderation link) and Director of Studies are layered grants on the same account: conflict moderation, unlock, and term close. Signs in to the app only.

threats.title: Password guessing against a teacher account
threats.description:
An attacker tries passwords for a known teacher email at POST /api/login until one works, then holds a token that reads the whole institution and can grade anything.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Two login rate limits apply together: five a minute per email and address, and twenty a minute per address (AppServiceProvider, RateLimiter 'login'). A wrong password and a deactivated account get the same answer, so the response does not confirm an account exists (LoginController; AuthenticationTest). Residual: teachers have no second factor and there is no lockout beyond the rate limit.

threats.title: Someone else uses a signed-in device as the teacher
threats.description:
A colleague, a student, or a thief picks up an unlocked or shared phone on which a teacher is signed in. The stored token speaks for the teacher with no further check, so that person can read every record and enter or change marks under the teacher's name.

CVSS:3.1/AV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated in the app. Device tokens have no expiry (config/sanctum.php, expiration null) and the app has no idle lock or re-authentication. What exists: an admin can revoke a teacher's devices in the panel, and EnsureAccountIsActive stops a deactivated account's token. Proposed for 5.3: a token lifetime with renewal on sync, and a password prompt before finalize and conflict resolution.

threats.title: A teacher denies entering or changing a mark
threats.description:
After a disputed result, a teacher claims they never made an edit, or that it was made at another time.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: The author of a write is the token's user, never a payload field: last_edited_by is server-owned and a payload carrying it is invalid (SyncPush, SERVER_OWNED). Every decided push is recorded in sync_mutations with user, verdict, payload hash, and the server's received_at, and that table refuses updates and deletes (SyncMutation, booted). Residual: the record names an account, not a person, so it is only as strong as the device threat above.

data.name:
App shell cache
(Workbox precache)
data.description: Precached JavaScript, CSS, and self-hosted fonts, so the app starts with no connection. Whatever is cached here is the code that handles the token and the marks.

threats.title: Cached app code is replaced on the device
threats.description:
Someone with control of the browser profile replaces the precached JavaScript, so the app the teacher opens offline is not the one that was deployed.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated, and not something the app can prevent: whoever controls the browser controls the code it runs. The server's checks hold regardless, since it trusts nothing the client sends. Recommended treatment: accept, and record it as a stated assumption that the device's browser is not compromised.

data.name:
PWA
(React app and
service worker)
data.description: The screens, the router, and the Workbox service worker. Reads the local store; every write goes to the outbox first. Makes the online-only calls itself: login, unlock, term close, Reports, the assistant, and report card download.

threats.title: Injected script runs inside the app
threats.description:
A cross-site scripting flaw, a compromised dependency, or a malicious browser extension runs script in the app's origin. That script can read the bearer token and every local record from IndexedDB, and can queue mutations as the teacher.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated. React escapes rendered text and the source uses no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and there are no remote scripts, fonts, or images (AGENTS.md, Frontend rules). Not mitigated: no Content-Security-Policy is sent, neither as a meta tag in frontend/index.html nor as a CloudFront response headers policy (infra/production/cdn.tf). Proposed for 5.3: a strict CSP (self only) set at CloudFront.

threats.title: A modified client performs actions the interface hides
threats.description:
A teacher edits the client, or calls the API directly, to finalize an assessment that is not theirs, resolve a conflict they are not party to, or act as HOD or Director of Studies.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Every permission is decided on the server; the interface only hides what would be refused. Assessment lifecycle: AssessmentPolicy (creator or assigned teacher). Conflicts: ConflictPolicy, with the actor taken from the token. In a push, authorization runs before the version rules (SyncPush::decide), so an unauthorized entry is answered forbidden. Tests: AssessmentPolicyTest, SyncPushConflictCommandsTest, SyncPushFinalizeTest.

data.name:
Session
(Dexie: sessions)
data.description: The Sanctum bearer token and the signed-in user, in IndexedDB. Tokens carry the sync ability and have no expiry (config/sanctum.php); they end at logout, deactivation, or revocation by an admin.

threats.title: The bearer token is read from the device
threats.description:
Malware, another user of the same computer account, a copied browser profile, or injected script reads the token from the sessions store. It is stored as plain text and works from any machine until revoked.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated on the device: a browser offers a web app no protected key store, and the token must be readable offline. Limits on the damage: revocation at logout and by an admin, and EnsureAccountIsActive on every request. The missing control is expiry: a stolen token never ages out (config/sanctum.php). Proposed for 5.3: a token lifetime.

threats.title: The stored session is edited to claim another user or role
threats.description:
A user edits the session record in IndexedDB to change the user id or the roles it lists.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: The server never reads identity or roles from the device: the institution and the actor come from the token (docs/spec/sync-protocol.md, Authorization and scoping). An edited session changes only what the local interface shows.

data.name:
Outbox
(Dexie: outbox)
data.description: Unsettled local writes (ADR 0011): one entry per mutation with a client mutation id, base version, and changed fields only.

threats.title: A forged base version is used to overwrite a newer edit
threats.description:
A teacher edits an outbox entry's baseVersion so that their value replaces a colleague's later one without a conflict being raised.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: A base ahead of the server is invalid; a base behind it goes to rule 4, which merges only disjoint fields and otherwise raises a conflict; only a base equal to the current version applies (SyncPush::decide, StaleBase; SyncPushConflictsTest). Stating the current version does let any teacher overwrite a mark, which is the access model's choice (marks are unrestricted), not a bypass: the write is versioned, logged, and attributed to that teacher.

threats.title: A queued entry carries fields the server owns
threats.description:
An entry is edited to include version, institutionId, lastEditedBy, createdBy, or receivedAt, to move a row to another school or attribute an edit to someone else.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Rejected outright as invalid, not silently stripped, and so is any unknown field name (SyncPush::envelope; SyncPushTest, 'a server-owned field is invalid'). institution_id is also immutable at the model (BelongsToInstitution, updating hook).

threats.title: The device clock is set wrong to backdate an edit
threats.description:
A teacher changes the device's clock so an edit appears to predate a deadline or another teacher's edit.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Order is never decided by time. Conflicts are detected by a stale base version (ADR 0001), and the device's time travels only as the informational `at`; the server's own received_at is what the log trusts (docs/spec/sync-protocol.md, Audit timestamps).

threats.title: Unsynced work is tied to one browser profile
threats.description:
A teacher's queued marks exist only in that browser until a sync succeeds. Clearing site data, or reinstalling the browser, discards them with no warning from the app.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: the Sync screen shows pending entries, and failed entries keep their values. Nothing warns before data is cleared, which the app cannot intercept. Recommended treatment: accept, with user guidance to sync before handing a device on.

data.name:
Local records
(Dexie tables)
data.description: The device's copy of the institution: students (name, gender, date of birth), enrolments, users (name, email), marks, results, conflicts, comments, report rows, and notifications. Any teacher reads everything in the institution, so the copy is institution-wide. Not encrypted beyond what the device itself provides.

threats.title: A lost or stolen device exposes the whole school's records
threats.description:
Each device holds every student's name, gender, date of birth, marks, and remarks for the institution, not only the teacher's own classes, because read access is institution-wide. Whoever takes the device and gets past its lock screen has all of it.

CVSS:3.1/AV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated in the app: the local store is not encrypted beyond what the device provides, and there is no remote wipe. An admin can revoke the device's token, which stops further pulls but does not remove what is already there. Proposed: guidance that devices use a screen lock, and a decision in the LINDDUN pass on whether a device needs the whole institution.

threats.title: Records stay on the device after sign-out
threats.description:
A teacher signs out of a shared computer. Sign-out clears the session only (performSignOut, authSession.ts); the teacher's local database remains (localDatabaseFor keeps one per user). The next person at that browser can open it in the developer tools.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated. Keeping the database is deliberate where the outbox still holds unsynced work, but nothing removes it once the outbox is empty. Proposed for 5.3: delete the user's local database at sign-out when the outbox has nothing pending, and warn before signing out with unsynced entries.

threats.title: Local records are edited to show false marks
threats.description:
A user edits marks or an assessment's status directly in IndexedDB, bypassing the outbox.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: The local copy is never authoritative. Only outbox entries are pushed, and each is decided by the server against its own row. An edit that bypasses the outbox changes what that one device displays and nothing else; the next pull of that record replaces it.

threats.title: The browser evicts the local store and unsynced marks are lost
threats.description:
On a device short of storage, the browser may evict the origin's IndexedDB. Marks entered offline and not yet pushed exist nowhere else.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: the app does not request persistent storage (no navigator.storage.persist call in frontend/src). Proposed for 5.3: request persistence at sign-in and show the answer on the Sync screen.

data.description: Our own code (ADR 0006): drains the outbox to POST /sync, pulls the change log from GET /sync by cursor, applies verdicts, and reconciles conflicts into the local store.

data.name: CloudFront
data.description: The one public HTTPS address. Serves the PWA from S3, and forwards /api, /admin, and the panel's assets to the host uncached, adding the origin secret header.

Auth and
Online APIs

data.name:
Sync API
(GET and POST
/sync)
data.description: The server half of the contribution. Push: idempotency by mutation id, version check, field-level merge, conflict raising, and accept or reject verdicts. Pull: sync_changes by cursor. Institution and actor come from the token, never the payload; server-owned fields in a payload are invalid.

threats.title: A deactivated or revoked account keeps syncing
threats.description:
A teacher who has left the school, or whose device was reported lost, still holds a token issued earlier.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: EnsureAccountIsActive runs on every authenticated route and refuses a deactivated account, so the token stops at once and not only at the next login; an admin can revoke a teacher's devices. Both sync verbs also require the token's sync ability (routes/api.php; SyncPullTest, SyncPushTest).

threats.title: A teacher reads or writes another school's records
threats.description:
A teacher of school A sends record ids, or an institutionId, belonging to school B in a push, or pulls with a tampered cursor, to cross the tenant boundary in the shared database.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The institution comes only from the token (ResolveInstitution), and every model carries a global scope that returns nothing when no institution is resolved inside a request (CurrentInstitution, fail closed). SyncPush refuses to run unless the request is resolved to the user's institution. Another school's id behaves as unknown: forbidden. The pull cursor is unsigned on purpose, since it can only misdirect the caller's own sync (SyncCursor). Tests: InstitutionScopeTest, SyncPullTest ('another institution never appears'), SyncPushTest ('a create whose id exists in another institution is forbidden').

threats.title: A create reveals that an id exists in another school
threats.description:
Primary keys are global, so a create at base version 0 is refused as forbidden only when the id already exists in another institution. A caller could use that difference to test whether an id exists elsewhere.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Accepted in the specification, and recorded here so the acceptance is visible: ids are unguessable UUIDs, and the answer reveals existence only, never content (docs/spec/sync-protocol.md, Authorization and scoping). Recommended treatment: accept.

threats.title: A mark is written into a finalized assessment
threats.description:
A device that was offline when an assessment was finalized, or a teacher acting deliberately, pushes a mark edit that would change results already final.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The handler locks the assessment row first and rejects the entry as edit-blocked before the mark's own version is considered, and the teacher gets an edit-blocked notification (MarkPushHandler::check; docs/spec/workflow.md; SyncPushFinalizeTest). Unlocking is a separate online action for an HOD or Director of Studies.

threats.title: A mark is pushed with references that do not belong together
threats.description:
An entry names a student who is not in the class, a criterion from another subject, a score above the criterion's maximum, or an id that is not the cell's own.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Checked on creation: the record id must be the deterministic UUIDv5 of the cell, the assessment, student, and criterion must resolve inside the institution, the student must be enrolled in the assessment's class and year, and the criterion must belong to its subject; the cell is validated against the criterion's maximum (MarkPushHandler::creation; SyncPushMarksTest).

threats.title: A mutation is replayed or its id reused
threats.description:
A dropped response makes a device resend, or someone resends a captured request, or reuses a known mutation id with different content.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Each mutation id is decided once and recorded (sync_mutations). A resend with the same payload hash gets the stored outcome and writes nothing; the same id with a different payload is invalid; an id first used by another user or school is invalid and reveals nothing of what was stored (SyncPush::replayOf; SyncPushTest, 'a resend of an accepted entry is replayed').

threats.title: A push claims to act as another user
threats.description:
An entry sets finalizedBy, a proposal's byId, or an acceptance's acceptedById to a colleague's id, to finalize or settle a conflict in their name.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: A field naming who performed this mutation must equal the token's user, or the entry is invalid; a field referring to earlier history must match what the server already holds (docs/spec/sync-protocol.md, the two-part rule; ConflictPushHandler; SyncPushConflictCommandsTest).

threats.title: A pull returns credentials or another user's notifications
threats.description:
The change log is institution-wide, so a careless serialisation could send password hashes, authenticator secrets, or another teacher's personal notifications to every device.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Hidden attributes never enter the sync log, so no device receives them (User model; SyncPullTest, 'never a hidden attribute'). Notifications are filtered to the caller on pull and on push (SyncPull::fromLog; NotificationPushHandler; SyncPullTest, 'notifications are pulled only by the user they belong to').

threats.title: One account floods the sync endpoints
threats.description:
Any teacher token can call GET and POST /api/sync without limit. Each push entry takes the institution's advisory lock, so a steady stream of 100-entry batches delays every other teacher's push in that school; each rejected entry also writes a sync_mutations row, so the log grows without bound; and a full bootstrap pull can be requested repeatedly.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated. No rate limit applies to these routes: the API group has no throttle (bootstrap/app.php does not enable it), and only the login and assistant limiters are defined (AppServiceProvider). What bounds a single request: 100 entries per batch (SyncPushController), a 10 MB body (deploy/nginx.conf), and a pull limit of 1000. Proposed for 5.3: a per-user limiter on both sync verbs, generous enough for a device draining a long offline outbox.

threats.title: Reads leave no record
threats.description:
A token, stolen or not, pulls the whole institution's records. Afterwards nothing in the application shows which account pulled, when, or how much.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated in the application: pushes are recorded in sync_mutations but pulls are not recorded anywhere, and the token row holds only a last-used time. Proposed: decide in the LINDDUN pass whether a pull record is wanted, since it is itself personal data about teachers.

data.name:
Accounts and tokens
(Postgres)
data.description: users (name, email, password hash, kind, directs_studies, deactivated_at), personal_access_tokens (hashed), panel sessions, and admins' authenticator secrets and recovery codes.
data.reasonOutOfScope: Modelled in diagram 2. API, accounts, and back office

data.name:
Domain tables
(Postgres)
data.description: Every institution's rows in one database, separated by institution_id under an Eloquent global scope: students, enrolments, classes, subjects, criteria, assessments, marks, conflicts, results, comments, reports, terms, term_closures, notifications, and unlock_notes. Soft deletes throughout. RDS, single zone, seven days of backups.

threats.title: Two concurrent writes silently overwrite each other
threats.description:
Two devices push to the same record at the same moment, and the later write replaces the earlier with no conflict raised: the lost update the project exists to prevent.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Three layers. Each entry runs in its own transaction behind the institution's advisory lock (SyncLog::transaction). The record is locked before it is read (lockRecord). And the UPDATE itself requires the row's version to equal the one read, so a write against a moved row changes nothing (Syncable; ADR 0001). The multi-device simulation exercises this (simulation/, ADR 0006).

threats.title: The database is read directly or from a backup
threats.description:
Someone reaches PostgreSQL without going through the application, or obtains a snapshot.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: The instance is not publicly accessible and is encrypted at rest, with access by security group from the host only (infra/production/database.tf: publicly_accessible false, storage_encrypted true). Its password is created and rotated by RDS in Secrets Manager and never passes through the repository (ADR 0015, decision 5).

data.name:
Sync logs
(sync_changes,
sync_mutations)
data.description: Append-only. sync_changes is the pull cursor and holds every changed field of every record; sync_mutations records every decided push with user, payload hash, verdict, the device's claimed time, and the server's received time.

threats.title: The change log is altered to hide an edit
threats.description:
Someone with database access, or a defect in server code, updates or deletes rows of sync_changes, so a past change to a mark no longer appears in the history that conflicts and audits rely on.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated. sync_mutations refuses updates and deletes at the model, but sync_changes has no such guard, and neither is protected in the database itself: the application's own database user can rewrite both. Proposed for 5.3: the same model guard on SyncChange, and a database rule or trigger that refuses UPDATE and DELETE on both tables.

threats.title: The logs grow without limit
threats.description:
sync_changes and sync_mutations are append-only and never pruned. Over years, or under the flooding threat above, they fill a small database instance.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: no retention or compaction exists. The indexes keep reads fast as the tables grow (docs/spec/data-model.md), and the budget alarm would show the cost. Proposed: a stated retention for sync_mutations and a compaction rule for sync_changes, decided together with the LINDDUN pass.

threats.title: A first visit is downgraded to HTTP
threats.description:
On a hostile network, a teacher's first request to the site is intercepted before the redirect to HTTPS, and they are served a look-alike sign-in page that collects their password.

Proposed for 5.3: HSTS in a CloudFront response headers policy, together with the CSP.

School admin
(back office)
data.description: An admin account: secretary, registrar, or bursar. Signs in to the Filament panel only, with an authenticator app in production. Writes the roster, accounts, role grants, and the term calendar. Does no academic work and never holds a device token.

threats.title: An admin's password is guessed or reused
threats.description:
An attacker obtains an admin's password, by guessing or from a breach elsewhere, and signs in to the panel, where one account can change every school record and every teacher's access.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: In production the panel requires an authenticator app at sign-in, with recovery codes, so a password alone is not enough (AdminPanelProvider, multiFactorAuthentication required when the app is in production). The panel's sign-in is rate limited separately from the API's, passwords are at least twelve characters, and every failure reads the same (AdminPanelTest, 'the panel login is rate limited', 'fail the same way').

threats.title: An admin denies a change made in the panel
threats.description:
A student record is altered, a teacher is given the Director of Studies grant, or a teacher's devices are revoked, and afterwards nobody can show which admin did it.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated. A panel write goes through Syncable, so sync_changes records what changed and when, but the log row has no actor column (SyncLog::append), and revoking tokens writes nothing at all. Only the term calendar records who acted (terms.opened_by, ended_by). Proposed for 5.3: an actor on sync_changes, or a small admin action log, covering grants, deactivation, and device revocation.

threats.title: An admin gives themselves academic authority
threats.description:
Admin and teacher accounts are separate so that the back office cannot alter results (ADR 0014). An admin can still create a teacher account, grant it Director of Studies, sign in to the app with it, and then unlock assessments and change marks.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated by design: the panel has one gate, an active admin account, with no per-action approval (ADR 0009, decision 3). The separation stops accidents, not a determined admin. What would expose it is the missing audit record above. Recommended treatment: accept the trust in admins, and add the audit record so the act is at least visible.

data.name: CloudFront
data.description: The one public HTTPS address. Serves the PWA from S3, and forwards /api, /admin, and the panel's assets to the host uncached, adding the origin secret header.

threats.title: The site is flooded from the internet
threats.description:
Anyone can send requests to the public address. Requests for /api and /admin are never cached, so each one reaches a single small host and its single small database.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: CloudFront absorbs network-level floods, static files are served from the edge, and the login and assistant routes have their own limits. Not mitigated: there is no web application firewall or rate rule at the edge (infra/production/cdn.tf), and no general limit in the application. Proposed for 5.3: the per-user limiter from diagram 1, and a rate-based rule at the edge if the pilot goes public.

threats.title: One user's API response is served to another from the cache
threats.description:
A shared cache that stored an authenticated response would hand one teacher's data, or one school's, to the next caller of the same address.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Caching is disabled for every path sent to the host, and all viewer headers are forwarded (infra/production/cdn.tf: the CachingDisabled policy on the API paths). Only the static frontend is cached.

threats.title: The panel or the app is framed by another site
threats.description:
A hostile page loads the admin panel in an invisible frame and tricks a signed-in admin into clicking a control, such as deactivating an account.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors directive is sent, since no response headers policy exists. The session cookie's SameSite setting of lax limits what a framed cross-site page can do, but it is not a guarantee. Proposed for 5.3: frame-ancestors 'none' in the same headers policy as the CSP and HSTS.

data.name: nginx
data.description: On the application host. Refuses any request without CloudFront's secret header, then hands off to PHP-FPM. The host's security group accepts HTTP only from CloudFront's published address range.

threats.title: The host is reached directly, around CloudFront
threats.description:
An attacker finds the host's public address and sends requests straight to it, skipping HTTPS and anything enforced at the edge.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L
threats.mitigation: The host's security group accepts port 80 only from CloudFront's origin-facing address list (infra/production/network.tf), and nginx returns 403 to any request without the secret header CloudFront adds (deploy/nginx.conf). The header is the real gate, since that address list admits every CloudFront customer; it is generated by Terraform, and it travels unencrypted on the leg recorded below.

threats.title: A forged X-Forwarded-For header evades the login limit
threats.description:
The login rate limit is keyed by client address. A caller who could choose the address the application sees could reset the limit at will.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Laravel is set to trust only the proxy that connected, which is CloudFront, so the client address is the one CloudFront appended and a value the caller supplies is ignored (bootstrap/app.php, trustProxies). Verified by reading the configuration, not by a test against a deployed host.

threats.title: The host's operating system is compromised
threats.description:
A vulnerability in the operating system, nginx, or PHP gives an attacker a shell on the one host that holds the application's settings and reaches the database.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: No SSH is exposed; administration is through Session Manager (network.tf, server.tf). Security updates install unattended (deploy/apt-auto-upgrades.conf), the root volume is encrypted, the instance metadata service requires session tokens, and the host's role can read only its own parameters (server.tf).

data.name:
Admin panel
(Filament, /admin)
data.description: Server-rendered back office with its own session guard (ADRs 0009 and 0014). The only writer of students, enrolments, classes, subjects, criteria, accounts, role grants, token revocation, and terms.

threats.title: A teacher account reaches the admin panel
threats.description:
A teacher signs in at /admin with their own password, or reuses a device token there, to manage accounts and grants.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: The panel's gate is an active admin account, asked on every request and not only at sign-in, and the panel uses its own session guard, so a device token is not a panel credential and a panel session is not an API one (User::canAccessPanel; AdminPanelTest, 'a non-admin cannot reach the panel', 'a panel session is not an API credential').

threats.title: An admin of one school reaches another school's records
threats.description:
An admin edits a record id in the address, or a Livewire update request, to list or change another institution's students and accounts.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The institution scope is applied as persistent panel middleware, so the first page load and every Livewire update after it are scoped to the admin's institution (AdminPanelProvider; AdminPanelTest, 'every Livewire request of the panel is scoped too', 'another institution's record is a 404 by its id').

threats.title: A forged request acts with an admin's session
threats.description:
A signed-in admin visits a hostile page that submits a form to the panel in the background.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The panel runs Laravel's request forgery protection on every state-changing request, and the session cookie is HTTP-only, secure, and SameSite lax (AdminPanelProvider middleware; config/session.php; deploy/release.sh sets SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE).

threats.title: A setup change silently alters recorded results
threats.description:
An admin lowers a marking criterion's maximum, or removes it, after marks were entered against it, which would change every result computed from them.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: A criterion that has marks keeps its maximum and cannot be removed; only its name can be corrected (docs/spec/access-model.md, What admin accounts do; AdminPanelTest, 'a criterion with marks keeps its maximum'). Accounts are deactivated, never deleted, so history keeps its references.

threats.title: The school is locked out of its own panel
threats.description:
An admin deactivates themselves or the only other admin, leaving nobody who can manage accounts.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
threats.mitigation: An admin cannot deactivate themselves or the last active admin (User::deactivate; AdminPanelTest, 'an administrator cannot deactivate themselves').

An admin signs in at the API with their panel password to get a token, combining back office and academic powers in one credential.

threats.title: Response time reveals whether an email has an account
threats.description:
The login answers an unknown email without checking a password hash, and a known one after a slow hash check. Measuring the difference tells an attacker which addresses are real teacher accounts.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

threats.title: A teacher unlocks an assessment or closes a term without the grant
threats.description:
A teacher calls the unlock or term close route directly, to reopen final results or to issue report cards.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Unlock is allowed only to a Director of Studies or the HOD of the assessment's subject (AssessmentPolicy::unlock), and term close only to a Director of Studies (ADR 0014, decisions 3 and 5). Having created the assessment does not grant it (WriteEndpointsTest, 'unlock returns 403 for a teacher without the grant'; TermCloseTest).

threats.title: A route is called with another school's record id
threats.description:
A teacher puts another institution's assessment or report id in the address of an unlock or download request.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Route binding goes through the institution scope, so another school's record is simply not found (WriteEndpointsTest, 'unlock returns 404 for an assessment in another institution'; ReadEndpointsTest).

threats.title: An unlock cannot be attributed
threats.description:
Final results are reopened and changed, and the person who unlocked them denies it.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Each unlock writes an append-only unlock_notes row with the acting user taken from the token, never from the request, and a note is required once report cards exist (docs/spec/workflow.md, Unlock; WriteEndpointsTest, 'records the authenticated account rather than client-supplied audit fields').

threats.title: Read endpoints are unlimited and unpaged
threats.description:
GET /api/students and the other list routes return every row of the institution in one response, and can be called without limit by any token.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: the same missing API rate limit as on diagram 1, and no pagination on these lists (StudentsController). At a pilot school's size the cost is small. Proposed for 5.3: covered by the per-user limiter; pagination only if a school outgrows it.

A session cookie is captured, or an admin walks away from an office computer while signed in.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

threats.title: Traffic between CloudFront and the host is unencrypted
threats.description:
The leg from CloudFront to the host's public address is plain HTTP. It carries teachers' and admins' passwords, authenticator codes, bearer tokens, session cookies, every sync payload, and the origin secret itself. Anyone able to observe that path can read and alter all of it, and with the secret can call the host directly.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated; a known, recorded decision: a certificate needs a domain, and there is none yet (ADR 0015, decision 7). The path runs between CloudFront and an AWS address, which narrows who could observe it but does not encrypt it. Proposed before any real school's data is loaded: a domain, a certificate on the host, and origin_protocol_policy set to https-only, which the ADR already describes as a Terraform change.

data.name:
Report assistant
(/reports/assistant)
data.description: Runs the tool loop server-side (ADR 0013): scope gate, read-only analytics tools, structured output, grounding check, handle-to-name restoration, per-user rate limit. Templated stand-in when no model key is set.

threats.title: A question talks the assistant out of its job
threats.description:
A teacher types instructions into the question box: ignore your rules, answer about something else, write in the school's name, reveal student names, or compare teachers.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Enforced by code, not only by the prompt (ADR 0013, decision 3). A separate gate call with no tools and no report data classifies the question first and fails closed. The answering model has only read-only report tools: no web, no code, no SQL. Its answer must fit a schema, every number in it must appear in a tool result of the same request, and an unanswerable or ungrounded answer is replaced by one fixed reply (ReportAssistant, Grounding; ReportAssistantTest, 'the gate fails closed', 'an ungrounded figure'). A red-team evaluation set exists as a command (EvaluateAssistant).

threats.title: Text stored in the school's data steers the assistant
threats.description:
Tool results include assessment names, which any teacher writes freely. A name crafted as an instruction reaches the answering model inside a tool result, past the gate, which only judges the question, and could skew what a colleague is told about that report.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: the model can do nothing but answer, the grounding check still requires every figure to come from a tool, and an assessment name is limited in length. Not mitigated: no check treats stored text as untrusted before it reaches the model. Proposed: add this case to the evaluation set, and strip or quote assessment names in tool results if it succeeds.

threats.title: The assistant is pointed at another school or another scope
threats.description:
A caller sends another institution's stream, subject, or assessment id as the report scope, or asks the model to look somewhere else.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: The scope is validated against the caller's institution exactly as the report summary validates it, every tool runs under the institution scope, and no tool takes a stream, subject, year, or school from the model (ReportAssistantController; ADR 0013, decisions 1 and 7; ReportAssistantTest, 'the scope is the report's').

threats.title: Another user's conversation is read or continued
threats.description:
A caller sends a conversation id that belongs to a colleague, to read their questions or to plant earlier turns.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: History is held by the server and the client sends only the new question, so earlier turns cannot be forged. A conversation belongs to one user and one report scope; any other caller, or the same caller with other filters, starts afresh (Conversation::resume; ReportAssistantTest, 'history is held by the server').

threats.title: The assistant is used to run up the model bill
threats.description:
Every question is a live model call with up to twelve tool round trips. A script asking continuously would spend the school's budget and exhaust the provider's rate limit for everyone.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
threats.mitigation: A teacher is limited to ten questions a minute and sixty an hour, a question to 500 characters, tool calls to twelve, and each call has a timeout (AppServiceProvider, RateLimiter 'assistant'; ReportAssistant; ReportAssistantTest, 'a teacher is limited to ten questions a minute').

data.description: jobs and failed_jobs (payloads name records by id), comment_generations, and the cache table, which holds assistant conversations in handle form with the handle-to-student mapping until they expire.

threats.title: Assistant conversations outlive their expiry
threats.description:
A conversation's questions and its handle-to-student mapping are written to the cache table with a thirty minute expiry. The application stops reading them after that, but nothing deletes the rows.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: an expired row is never returned by the application, and the table is in the private, encrypted database. Not mitigated: there is no scheduler and no pruning command in the repository, so expired rows remain until overwritten. Proposed for 5.3: prune expired cache rows from the queue worker.

threats.title: A job's payload is altered or carries personal data
threats.description:
Queued jobs sit in a database table until a worker takes them, and failed ones stay in failed_jobs.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: A job carries only record ids and its institution, never names or marks, and is dispatched only by server code after the writing transaction commits (ADR 0007). The table is reachable only from the host.

data.name: Queue worker
data.description: Laravel queue on the database driver (ADR 0007). Submits and collects comment batches, renders report card PDFs with Dompdf, and writes them to S3.

threats.title: A stale job issues a report card for a cycle that was unwound
threats.description:
A comment is accepted, its report job is queued, and before the job finishes an unlock unwinds the term. The job would otherwise publish a card built on results that are no longer final.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The job rechecks at its final write, under the institution's lock, that the comment is still live and accepted, the term closure still live, and no card yet exists; otherwise it records nothing and deletes the object it wrote (GenerateReportCard; ReportCardTest, 'an unwind that lands while the PDF is being written'). A generation result is applied only to the latest generation of a live, pending comment (CommentGenerationTest).

threats.title: A job runs without an institution and sees every school
threats.description:
Outside a request the institution scope filters nothing, by design, so that seeders and commands work. A queued job that forgot to set its institution would read and write across every school.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Each job carries its institution and runs inside CurrentInstitution::actingFor, including its failure handlers; the binding is fresh per job on a worker (GenerateReportCard, SubmitCommentBatch, CollectCommentBatch; CommentGenerationTest, 'a job runs as its institution'). Residual: this is a convention each new job must follow, not something the framework enforces.

threats.title: Text in a name or remark injects markup into the PDF
threats.description:
A student's name or a teacher's remark containing HTML is rendered into the report card and changes its appearance, or makes the renderer fetch a remote file.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: The card is a Blade view with escaped output only, the renderer has remote loading disabled (GenerateReportCard::render, isRemoteEnabled false), and a remark is limited to 600 characters with no control characters (CommentPushHandler).

threats.title: Remarks are regenerated without limit
threats.description:
A class teacher or Director of Studies can send the regenerate command for a comment as often as they like while it is not accepted. Each one submits a new request to the model provider.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: regenerate has no count or rate limit, and the sync route it arrives on has none either (diagram 1). The damage is bounded by who may send it and by the batch price of a short remark. Proposed for 5.3: covered by the per-user sync limiter; a per-comment cap if cost shows it is needed.

data.name:
Report card PDFs
(S3 bucket)
data.description: One PDF per student per term, keyed reports/{institution}/{report}.pdf. Each carries the student's name, school, performance levels, and the teacher's remark. Read only through a ten minute presigned URL.

threats.title: Report cards are read from the bucket by someone outside the school
threats.description:
Each PDF names a child and their school and carries their levels and remark.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: The bucket is private with all public access blocked, readable and writable only by the host's role (infra/production/storage.tf). Keys are named by the report's id, never by the student, so a key reveals nothing and cannot be guessed. A download needs a presigned URL from the API, issued only inside the institution and valid for ten minutes (ReportsController; ReportCardTest, 'within the institution only').

threats.title: Superseded report cards are never deleted
threats.description:
When an unlock unwinds a term, its report rows are soft deleted and new cards are issued later, but the old PDFs stay in the bucket. Over time it accumulates cards that were withdrawn, each naming a child.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: a soft-deleted report cannot be downloaded through the API, and the bucket is private. Not mitigated: nothing removes the object (the only delete is for a job's own failed write, in GenerateReportCard), and the bucket has no lifecycle rule. Proposed: delete the object when its report is unwound, or a lifecycle rule; decide retention in the LINDDUN pass.

data.name:
Model provider
(Anthropic API)
data.description: Third party outside the school and outside Kenya. Receives comment prompts (levels and trends, no names) through the batch API and assistant questions with tool results (figures including percentages, students as handles) through the live API (ADRs 0012 and 0013).

threats.title: A student's name reaches the model provider in a question
threats.description:
The assistant replaces a roster student's name with a handle before either model sees the question. A name typed in lower case, misspelt, shared by two students, or belonging to someone off the roster is not caught, and leaves the school with whatever the teacher wrote about that child.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated, and documented as provisional: full names in any case and unshared name parts written with a capital are replaced; no school name is ever sent; tool results carry handles only (Handles::conceal; ADR 0013, decision 4; ReportAssistantTest, 'a student's name typed into the question reaches neither model'). The decision waits on the advisory about sending student data to a provider.

threats.title: The model writes something false or unsuitable
threats.description:
A generated remark invents a fact about a child, or an assistant answer states a wrong figure, and it is taken as the school's word.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: A generated remark is only a draft: a person must accept each one, there is no accept-all, and only an accepted remark produces a card (docs/spec/workflow.md, Comments). The comment prompt carries levels and trends only, so there is little to invent from. Assistant figures must match a tool result or the fixed reply is shown. Stand-in text is labelled as such.

data.name:

data.description: The report's scope and filters and the new question; the server holds the history.

threats.title: The assistant is called without a signed-in teacher
threats.description:
Someone calls the assistant route directly to query a school's results or spend its budget.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: The route sits behind the same token check and active-account check as every API route, and without a model key configured it answers 503 and the app shows its labelled stand-in (routes/api.php; ReportAssistantTest, 'without a key there is no assistant').

threats.title: A job is dispatched for a change that never committed

A term close or an accepted remark fails after its job was queued, and the worker acts on rows that do not exist or hold other values.

threats.title: Identifiable student data is sent to the provider by the assistant

threats.title: A presigned report card link is passed on
threats.description:
The link is the only credential for the PDF. Anyone it is forwarded to, or who finds it in a browser history or a chat within ten minutes, can download that child's card without signing in, and the download is not recorded by the application.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: the link expires after ten minutes, is issued only to a signed-in teacher of the institution, and is fetched over HTTPS. Not mitigated: within that window it works for anyone, and no record is kept of who asked for which card. Recommended treatment: accept the ten minute window; record download requests if the LINDDUN pass calls for it.

diagrams.title: 4. Deployment
diagrams.description: How code and settings reach production. Every merge to main deploys (ADR 0015).

data.name: AWS account, af-south-1
data.description: Production as declared in infra/ (ADR 0015). Reached from the internet only through CloudFront.

data.name: Teacher device
data.description: A teacher's own phone or laptop. Not managed by the school, may be shared or lost, and holds a copy of the institution's data. The server treats every value that leaves it as a claim.

data.name:
GitHub Actions
(deploy and infra)
data.description: Workflows of this repository, signed in to AWS through OIDC. Covers both the deploy workflow and the Terraform plan and apply. The apply role is an administrator; what guards it is that only a run on main can assume it (ADR 0015).

threats.title: A leaked cloud key gives control of the AWS account
threats.description:
A long-lived AWS access key stored as a repository secret leaks through a log, a fork, or a laptop, and works from anywhere until someone notices.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: No AWS key exists to leak: workflows sign in through GitHub's OIDC, AWS checks the token's audience and subject, and the credentials last for the run only (infra/bootstrap/main.tf; ADR 0015, decision 5). GitHub holds role names, not keys.

threats.title: The application deploy runs as an account administrator
threats.description:
The deploy workflow needs to copy a file to one bucket, send one command to one host, sync one bucket, and invalidate one distribution. It assumes the apply role, which has AdministratorAccess because Terraform creates roles. Anything that subverts a deploy run therefore holds the whole account: every school's data, the database, and the ability to delete production.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: only a run on main can assume the role (OIDC subject ref:refs/heads/main), and main accepts only reviewed merges (CONTRIBUTING.md, the branch ruleset). Not mitigated: the deploy is not separated from Terraform's apply. Proposed for 5.3: a third, narrow deploy role holding only the actions listed above, for deploy.yml.

threats.title: A third-party action is replaced upstream
threats.description:
The workflows use actions by version tag (aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4, shivammathur/setup-php@v2, hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3, and others). A tag can be moved, so a compromised action maintainer can run their own code inside a deploy, with the administrator role's credentials in the same job.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: no action is pinned to a commit SHA. Proposed for 5.3: pin each action to a full commit SHA, with the tag in a comment, and let Dependabot propose updates.

threats.title: A compromised dependency ships in a release
threats.description:
A package in composer.json or package.json, or one of their dependencies, publishes a malicious version, which is then built into the API or the PWA and runs with the school's data.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Partly mitigated: releases install exactly the locked versions (composer install from composer.lock, npm ci from package-lock.json), so nothing changes without a lockfile change in a reviewed merge request. Not mitigated: no dependency audit runs in check.yml and no Dependabot configuration exists, so a known vulnerable version is not flagged. Proposed for 5.3: composer audit and npm audit in check, and Dependabot for security updates.

threats.title: Any pull request can read production secrets and report cards
threats.description:
The plan role may be assumed by any workflow of this repository running for a pull request (OIDC subject pull_request), and it holds AWS ReadOnlyAccess, which includes reading every S3 object. A pull request runs the workflow files of its own branch, so a collaborator can add a step to a workflow and, before any review, read the Terraform state (which holds the Laravel key and the origin secret) and every report card PDF.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated. What limits it: forks do not receive an OIDC token, so only someone with push access to the repository can do this, and the state and reports buckets are otherwise private (ADR 0015, decisions 3 and 5). Proposed for 5.3: replace ReadOnlyAccess with a policy that can plan but denies s3:GetObject on the reports bucket and limits the state bucket to the state object; or restrict the plan role to workflow runs of infra.yml through the job_workflow_ref claim. To verify against AWS's current ReadOnlyAccess before relying on it.

threats.title: Nobody can tell which code was running when
threats.description:
After an incident, the team needs to know which commit was live on the host at a given moment, and who caused it to deploy.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N
threats.mitigation: Each deploy is a GitHub Actions run tied to a reviewed merge, the release directory on the host is named by commit, run, and attempt, and the Systems Manager command carries the commit in its comment (deploy.yml). AWS keeps 90 days of management events by default. Residual: no CloudTrail trail is declared in infra/, so nothing is kept beyond those 90 days.

threats.title: The PWA in its bucket is replaced
threats.description:
Whatever is in the frontend bucket becomes the code every teacher's device runs, with their token and the whole school's records.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: The bucket is private with public access blocked; only CloudFront may read it, through origin access control, and only the apply role may write it, from a run on main (infra/production/storage.tf). Residual: the apply role's breadth, recorded above.

(code on the host)
data.description: The Laravel application as deployed: the code every API request, panel page, and job runs. Replaced by each merge to main.

threats.title: The release archive is swapped in the bucket before the host unpacks it
threats.description:
The deploy uploads release.tar.gz to the reports bucket, under _releases/, then asks the host to download and unpack it and run deploy/release.sh as root. The application's own role may write any object in that bucket. Code that has already compromised the application (running as www-data) could replace the archive in that window and have its own script run as root.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: Not mitigated: the archive is not checked after download, and it shares a bucket the application can write. The window is short and needs an existing compromise of the application. Proposed for 5.3: have the workflow pass the archive's SHA-256 in the command and verify it on the host before unpacking; or stage releases in a bucket or prefix the application role cannot write.

threats.title: A broken release takes the API down
threats.description:
A release whose install, migration, or cache step fails, or that does not answer once live, leaves teachers unable to sync.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
threats.mitigation: Everything that can fail runs while the previous release is still serving; the switch is one atomic rename; and if a service will not reload or /up does not answer, release.sh switches back. Migrations are additive only, so the previous release works against the new schema, and the five newest releases are kept for a manual rollback (deploy/release.sh; ADR 0015, decision 4).

threats.title: An older commit deploys over a newer one
threats.description:
Two merges close together trigger two deploys that finish out of order, and production ends up running the older code against the newer schema.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
threats.mitigation: Deploys share one concurrency group, and a first attempt goes ahead only if its commit is still the tip of main; a run by hand must be on main with check passed on that commit (deploy.yml, the gate job).

threats.title: A release goes live on a vulnerable runtime
threats.description:
The host's PHP has a known remote code execution flaw, and a deploy makes the application live on it.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
threats.mitigation: release.sh refuses to deploy on PHP older than a stated minimum carrying the known fixes, and security updates install unattended (deploy/release.sh, step 0; deploy/apt-auto-upgrades.conf).

threats.title: The application's secrets are read on the host
threats.description:
The .env holds the database password, the Laravel key, and the model provider key, and is read by every PHP process.

CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
